chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Resetting the book without Chick Webb
summary: The week at the Savoy was spent cutting drum solos and reworking the opening numbers; Ella stayed the star as the band rebuilt.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: How long did you play the Savoy before you went on the road?

Well, we only played there about a week. I think (inaudible) just to reset the band, and add Bill Beeson to the band. And reset some of the arrangements, you know. Chick wasn't with us anymore so we had to reset his solos. I mean take out and add. You know, just reset the whole routine of what we're going to play. (Inaudible) a show, we have to reset everything, because Chick Webb was a big part of the band. And we had to rearrange the arrangements -- you know, take out a lot of the drummer solos, and do

We had to just turn around -- we wasn't going to do this, we're going to change this, we're going to change that, you know. Things like that. Wasn't much (inaudible) with Ella Fitzgerald. Ella would (inaudible). (inaudible) Come to a point where Ella is another attraction.

We had worked up to the point when she was a star. We had build -- like I told you before, we had started giving Ella pop -- (inaudible) Send her to make her pop. Send her straight pop with all the big pop songs. You remember I talked to you about that.
And her part -- we didn't have to do anything with her. She just stay where she was at. It was the band part we had to straighten out -- the opening.
Chick Webb had a big part in the opening -- the drums (inaudible) things. You know, (inaudible) Comes Charlie". "Clap Hands Here Nando
